subject.title: autoreview: secret-scanner false positives on identifier and member-expression values (e.g. `apiSecret: ctx.cloudinary.apiSecret`)

question: Should autoreview add syntax-aware safe-reference recognition for programming-language contexts, or retain the current scanner and provide a controlled redaction override?
rationale: The false positives are well supported, but a language-agnostic exemption could create secret-scanner false negatives across the mixed-language diffs autoreview processes.

options.title: Add syntax-aware references
options.body: Recognize pure identifiers and member expressions only when surrounding syntax provides strong code-context evidence, with negative regression coverage for YAML and shell-style assignments.

options.title: Add controlled redaction
options.body: Keep conservative detection but permit an explicit reviewed override that redacts flagged lines and marks the review input incomplete.

options.title: Allow all reference shapes
options.body: Treat identifier and dotted-member values as safe throughout scanned text, accepting broader false-negative risk in unquoted formats.

recommendation.title: Add syntax-aware references
recommendation.body: Recognize pure identifiers and member expressions only when surrounding syntax provides strong code-context evidence, with negative regression coverage for YAML and shell-style assignments.
